messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Just wanted to note that I am working with the newest release (2.1.6) and this error persists: I run timer() on files and if a bat call occurs too close to the end of the file, the output will have a start but not an end value.

Thanks,

On Tuesday, December 24, 2019 at 10:31:44 PM UTC+1 fot...@gmail.com wrote:
> Hello everybody,
>
> Can anybody help me on how to measure pitch variability in a wav file in R?
>
> Best,
> Fotis
>

> > > I have noticed when using the timer function with certain audio files the s.start and s.end positions appear to show the start and end positions of the pause rather than the signal. messages.subject: Optimizing timer() and ggspectro() parameters - odd behavior
messages.subject_clean: Optimizing timer() and ggspectro() parameters - odd behavior
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I'm using the timer() function to detect bat calls in my recordings. I'm having an issue with the parameter settings and wanted to ask for some advice regarding both the optimization of timer() and plotting parameters for ggspectro().

Problem:
My recordings were made in a sound-isolated chamber - so there's relatively little noise. For a given file, I will get pretty good identification of most calls, but then for some sections of the very same file there are tons of detections of simple noise and they are plotted as though noise is exceptionally high. Since the noise level is pretty uniform within each recording (~1 minute each), I don't quite understand this behavior.

My questions are:
1. Is the amplitude threshold in timer() relative to the whole file, or just the current sliding window?
2. Why would timer() identify calls from noise correctly in one section of the file and catch many false positives in another, if the energy levels are about the same?
3. Theoretically, what's the best strategy to detect calls using timer() if noise levels do vary within a single file?
4. Are the limits/colevels parameters in the ggspectro/spectro functions scaled to the rms or energy of the selected sample?

Sample Data & Output:
Below you will find my pipeline. Here you will also find an example sound file and the plotted spectrograms and detected calls output by the program below: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XMWspiV10mWUT4WrmXBAqq527N3Sr__e?usp=sharing
As you can see, some sections of the sound file are plotted by ggspectro as though background noise is very high, while other sections seem 'cleaner'. But if you open the sound file in a software like Audacity or Avisoft, there's not much difference. (E.g. minute 8.2-8.4 has an rms of -65.16 while the section 9-9.2 min has an rms of -65.19. But looking at the spectrograms plotted (file02_8 and file02_9, respectively), it appears as though the latter has much more noise and there are a ton of false positives.)

Pipeline:
# filter each sound file to desired freq range
wav.filt <- seewave::ffilter(wav@left, f = w...@samp.rate, from = 10000, to = 120000)

# get call data
call_data <- seewave::timer(wav.filt, f=w...@samp.rate,
                threshold = 1,
                dmin = 0.001,
                envt = 'abs',
                power = 1,
                msmooth = c(512,50), # window, overlap
                plot = FALSE)

# in case a call starts right at the end of the file but an end is not recorded, assume it ends at the end of the file and set the offset value

    if (length(call_data$s.start) > length(call_data$s.end) &
        dplyr::last(call_data$s.end)<dplyr::last(call_data$s.start)) {
        call_data$s.end <- c(call_data$s.end,length(wav@left)/w...@samp.rate)
        }

# weld into df and quantify onset intervals between calls

    calls <- data.frame(sig.start = call_data$s.start, sig.end = call_data$s.end) %>%
                        dplyr::rename(starts = sig.start,
                                      ends = sig.end) %>%
                        mutate(duration = call_data$s,
                               onset.interval = starts-dplyr::lag(starts)) %>%
                        mutate(min = filenum, .before = 1)

# plot the spectrogram of the file along with detected calls to ensure correct detections:

 checker <- calls[order(calls$starts),] %>% add_column(y.val = 95)
      graph.path <- file.path(results_path,'graphical_check')
        dir.create(graph.path,recursive = TRUE)

# plot in segments because 1 minute is way too long to see the details:
      segments <- seq(from = 0, to = length(wav@left)/w...@samp.rate, length.out = 50)

      for (i in 2:length(segments)) {
        curr_seg <- checker %>% dplyr::filter(min==as.character(filenum))
        curr_seg <-  curr_seg[which(curr_seg$starts<=segments[i] & curr_seg$starts>segments[i-1]), ]
        if (!nrow(curr_seg)==0) {
        seewave::ggspectro(wav.filt,
             tlim = c(segments[i-1],segments[i]),
             f = w...@samp.rate,
             wl = 512, ovlp = 50,
fastdisp = TRUE, palette = temp.colors,
                    noisereduction = TRUE)  +
                    geom_tile(mapping = aes(fill = amplitude)) +
                    geom_segment(data = curr_seg,
 mapping = aes(x = starts, y = y.val,                                                 xend = ends, yend = y.val,
                     color = "red"),                            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 2) +
                  scale_fill_continuous(name="Amplitude\n(dB)\n", limits=c(-70,0),
                    na.value="transparent", low="white", high="black") +
                    theme_bw() +
                    ggsave(file.path(graph.path,paste0('file',filenum,'_',i,'.png'))) }

Thank you so much in advance!
Ava

messages.subject: Start and end times of timer() result swapped, plus patch resolving the issue
messages.subject_clean: Start and end times of timer() result swapped, plus patch resolving the issue
messages.body_plain:
When an audio fragment is passed to `timer()`, starting with a signal of less than `dmin`, the result returned from the `timer()` call is wrong.
This pieces of code demonstrate and reproduce the issue. This shows a correct result (set `sf` to any sample frequency you prefer; e.g., `sf <- 16000` works):

```
> timer(c(rep(1, 0.1 * sf), rep(0, sf), rep(1, sf), rep(0, 0.1 * sf)), sf, dmin=0.05, plot=F)
$s
[1] 0.1000028 1.0000284

$p
[1] 1.00002841 0.09994034

$r
[1] 1.000057

$s.start
[1] 0.000000 1.100031

$s.end
[1] 0.1000028 2.1000597

$first
[1] "signal"
```

On the contrary, changing `dmin` to 0.2 reproduces the bug we encountered:

```
> timer(c(rep(1, 0.1 * sf), rep(0, sf), rep(1, sf), rep(0, 0.1 * sf)), sf, dmin=0.2, plot=F)
$s
[1] 1.1000313 0.1000028

$p
[1] 0.9999659

$r
[1] 1.200075

$s.start
[1] 0.000000 2.099997

$s.end
[1] 1.100031

$first
[1] "signal"
```

In particular, while `s` and `p` are correct, `s.start` and `s.end` are swapped (`s.start` should be +- 1.1, while `s.end` should be +- 2.1).

The reason for this bug seems to lie in the `if (wave2[1] == 1)` condition: `wave2` contains the signals/silence before it has been filtered on `dmin`, whereas `wave4` contains only signals longer than `dmin`. The following patch fixes the issue, to the best of my knowledge (if I have not overlooked another corner case?):

```
$ diff -u seewave.orig.r seewave.r
--- seewave.orig.r    2020-05-28 10:52:10.000000000 +0200
+++ seewave.r    2021-04-13 23:07:47.013635984 +0200
@@ -7648,7 +7648,7 @@
     npos <- length(positions)
     if(npos<=2) stop("It seems that the sound is continuous, there are not signal/pause events.")
     ## the wave starts with a pause
-    if (wave2[1] == 1) {
+    if (wave4[2] == 2) {
         first <- "pause"
         pause <- durations[seq(1, npos - 1, by = 2)]
         signal <- durations[seq(2, npos - 1, by = 2)]
@@ -7689,7 +7689,7 @@
             wave8[i] <- ((wave5[i] - wave5[i - 1])/2) + wave5[i -
                 1]
         }
-        if(wave2[1] == 1) {
+        if(wave4[2] == 2) {
             wave8.1 <- wave8[seq(2, npos, by = 2)]/f1
             wave8.2 <- wave8[seq(3, npos, by = 2)]/f1
         }  else {
```

Using this updated version of `seewave.r`, the previously failing example now works:

```
> source("seewave.r")
> timer(c(rep(1, 0.1 * sf), rep(0, sf), rep(1, sf), rep(0, 0.1 * sf)), sf, dmin=0.2, plot=F)
$s
[1] 0.9999659

$p
[1] 1.1000313 0.1000028

$r
[1] 0.8332812

$s.start
[1] 1.100031

$s.end
[1] 2.099997

$first
[1] "pause"
```

This issue seems like it might also be related to the "
Odd behavior in timer()" email thread at https://groups.google.com/g/seewave/c/KroqU5ag_-o

Thank you for providing the seewave library!

Kind regards
Yannick Jadoul (& Marianna Anichini)

messages.body_plain:
Dear Jerôme

Thank you very much for your reply! I will look forward to using this new version!

Meanwhile, I bumped into a minor related issue. Calling `timer()` on a audio fragment that ends on a signal, results in the last value of `s.end` missing:

```
> timer(c(rep(1, sf), rep(0, sf), rep(1, sf)), sf, plot=F)
$s
[1] 1.0000208 0.9999583

$p
[1] 1.000021

$r
[1] 1.999937

$s.start
[1] 0.000000 2.000042

$s.end
[1] 1.000021

$first
[1] "signal"
```

And the following even simpler example results in an error inside of `timer()`:

```
> timer(c(rep(0, sf), rep(1, sf)), sf, plot=F)
Error in seq.default(3, npos - 1, by = 2) : wrong sign in 'by' argument
```

If I understood the correctly, changing the following two lines assigning to `end.signal` to `end.signal <- positions[seq(..., npos, by = 2)]` (instead of `npos - 1`) fixes this issue and still gets other input correct:

```
> timer(c(rep(0, sf), rep(1, sf)), sf, plot=F)
$s
[1] 0.9999687

$p
[1] 1.000031

$r
[1] 0.9999375

$s.start
[1] 1.000031

$s.end
[1] 2

$first
[1] "pause"
```

If you agree with this issue and proposed solution, would it be possible to still include this fix as well?
Combined with the previous 2 changes, the full patch would look like this:

```

$ diff -u seewave.orig.r seewave.r
--- seewave.orig.r    2020-05-28 10:52:10.000000000 +0200

+++ seewave.r    2021-04-15 12:49:36.583457006 +0200
@@ -7648,12 +7648,12 @@

     npos <- length(positions)
     if(npos<=2) stop("It seems that the sound is continuous, there are not signal/pause events.")
     ## the wave starts with a pause
-    if (wave2[1] == 1) {
+    if (wave4[2] == 2) {
         first <- "pause"
         pause <- durations[seq(1, npos - 1, by = 2)]
         signal <- durations[seq(2, npos - 1, by = 2)]

         start.signal <- positions[seq(2, npos - 1, by = 2)]
-        end.signal <- positions[seq(3, npos - 1, by = 2)]
+        end.signal <- positions[seq(3, npos, by = 2)]
     }
     ## the wave starts with a signal
     else {
@@ -7661,7 +7661,7 @@
         pause <- durations[seq(2, npos - 1, by = 2)]
         signal <- durations[seq(1, npos - 1, by = 2)]
         start.signal <- positions[seq(1, npos - 1, by = 2)]
-        end.signal <- positions[seq(2, npos - 1, by = 2)]
+        end.signal <- positions[seq(2, npos, by = 2)]
     }
     ratio <- sum(signal)/sum(pause)
     timer <- list(s = signal, p = pause, r = ratio,

@@ -7689,7 +7689,7 @@
             wave8[i] <- ((wave5[i] - wave5[i - 1])/2) + wave5[i -

                 1]timer()

         }
-        if(wave2[1] == 1) {
+        if(wave4[2] == 2) {
             wave8.1 <- wave8[seq(2, npos, by = 2)]/f1
             wave8.2 <- wave8[seq(3, npos, by = 2)]/f1
         }  else {

```

Kind regards
Yannick Jadoul

> In particular, while `s` and `p` are correct, `s.start` and `s.end` are swapped (`s.start` should be +- 1.1, while `s.end` should be +- 2.1).
>
> The reason for this bug seems to lie in the `if (wave2[1] == 1)` condition: `wave2` contains the signals/silence before it has been filtered on `dmin`, whereas `wave4` contains only signals longer than `dmin`. The following patch fixes the issue, to the best of my knowledge (if I have not overlooked another corner case?):
>
> ```
> $ diff -u seewave.orig.r seewave.r
> --- seewave.orig.r    2020-05-28 10:52:10.000000000 +0200
> +++ seewave.r    2021-04-13 23:07:47.013635984 +0200
> @@ -7648,7 +7648,7 @@
>      npos <- length(positions)
>      if(npos<=2) stop("It seems that the sound is continuous, there are not signal/pause events.")
>      ## the wave starts with a pause
> -    if (wave2[1] == 1) {
> +    if (wave4[2] == 2) {
>          first <- "pause"
>          pause <- durations[seq(1, npos - 1, by = 2)]
>          signal <- durations[seq(2, npos - 1, by = 2)]
> @@ -7689,7 +7689,7 @@
>              wave8[i] <- ((wave5[i] - wave5[i - 1])/2) + wave5[i -
>                  1]
>          }
> -        if(wave2[1] == 1) {
> +        if(wave4[2] == 2) {
>              wave8.1 <- wave8[seq(2, npos, by = 2)]/f1
>              wave8.2 <- wave8[seq(3, npos, by = 2)]/f1
>          }  else {
> ```
>
> Using this updated version of `seewave.r`, the previously failing example now works:
>
> ```
> > source("seewave.r")
> > timer(c(rep(1, 0.1 * sf), rep(0, sf), rep(1, sf), rep(0, 0.1 * sf)), sf, dmin=0.2, plot=F)
> $s
> [1] 0.9999659
>
> $p
> [1] 1.1000313 0.1000028
>
> $r
> [1] 0.8332812
>
> $s.start
> [1] 1.100031
>
> $s.end
> [1] 2.099997
>
> $first
> [1] "pause"
> ```
>
> This issue seems like it might also be related to the "
> Odd behavior in timer()" email thread at https://groups.google.com/g/seewave/c/KroqU5ag_-o
>
>
> Thank you for providing the seewave library!
>
> Kind regards
> Yannick Jadoul (& Marianna Anichini)
